best_for: Staff and admins at organizations that self-host ownCloud and want company files synced to Windows and Mac desktops, with placeholders so large shares do not fill the disk.

points.title: You need an ownCloud server
points.text: The desktop app only syncs with a server your organization or provider runs. It is not a storage service by itself.

points.title: 7.x talks only to Infinite Scale
points.text: From version 7.0 the app works only with ownCloud Infinite Scale and dropped support for the older ownCloud Server. If your company still runs ownCloud Server, stay on the 6.x client.

points.title: Why Windows here is on 6.0
points.text: The Windows listing here tops out at 6.0.3, the line that still connects to ownCloud Server, while the Mac listing is on 7.1.1. Check which server you use before you pick a version.

points.title: Files appear before they download
points.text: Virtual files show your whole share as placeholders and fetch a file only when you open it. That keeps a large share from filling a small laptop drive.

points.title: Several accounts and quick sharing
points.text: You can add more than one account, and the file manager's right-click menu gains options to create public and private share links.

points.title: Open source and free to install
points.text: The client is under GPL 2.0 and costs nothing. Any cost sits with the server plan your organization runs.

points.title: System floor
points.text: The 7.1 docs list Windows 10 version 1809 or later, and say external drives holding synced data must be NTFS. Windows comes as a 64-bit MSI that installs for all users; the Mac has separate Intel and Apple Silicon packages.

points.title: No Linux listing here
points.text: This site lists Windows and macOS. ownCloud offers an AppImage for Linux on its own site. The Windows listing keeps 15 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
